name: Centro de Datos Alcalá (Alcalá Data Center)

profile.reading:
This is the Alcala Data Center campus in Alcala de Henares, in the Madrid metropolitan area close to Madrid-Barajas airport. OpenStreetMap still records Telefonica as the operator, and the campus was built as a Telefonica facility, but it is run today by Nabiax, the Spanish data centre operator formed when Telefonica's data centre portfolio passed to new ownership. Nabiax publishes current figures for the site, and they correct a figure this registry previously carried.

The campus consists of two buildings. Nabiax gives the site 22.3 megawatts of IT power across its first two completed phases, with expansion potential to 100 megawatts in the medium term, which it describes as making Alcala the largest data centre campus in Spain. The 100 megawatt number is expansion potential, and it is also the rating Telefonica's own published fact sheet gives for the dedicated electrical substation serving the site. Neither of those is an IT load. The IT load figure is the 22.3 megawatts, and this registry now states the distinction plainly rather than presenting a substation rating as installed IT capacity.

The first building, ADC 1, opened in 2013, holds seven IT rooms across about 4,800 square metres, has generators in a 2N topology, chillers in 2N with air handling units at N plus 2, and three separate fibre entry paths. It is certified to Uptime Institute Tier IV. The second building, ADC 2, opened in 2021 with six IT rooms across about 6,000 square metres, generators at N plus 1, chillers and air handling units at N plus 1, and three fibre entry paths, designed and built to Tier III standard. Together the campus carries more than 10,000 square metres of built IT space in a fully carrier neutral ecosystem, and Nabiax describes it as the national reference site for hyperscale customers.

Telefonica's own fact sheet for the site gives complementary detail. The building complex totals about 75,000 square metres, of which around 15,000 square metres is usable technical space, organised into independent modular rooms of about 681 square metres each. Cooling uses free cooling with isothermal cisterns, backed by diesel standby generation. The site is described as running entirely on renewable electricity. Certifications listed across the two operators include Uptime Institute Tier IV Gold for 99.995 percent uptime on the first building, alongside PCI DSS, ISO 20000, ISO 27001, ISO 14001, LEED, and Spanish data protection and Esquema Nacional de Seguridad compliance.

Telefonica marketed the site for managed and outsourced cloud infrastructure, hosting and disaster recovery across Spain and Europe, with synchronous replication to two of its other data centres and connectivity to roughly 100 points of presence in more than 40 countries over about 45,000 kilometres of fibre. Alcala de Henares has long been a university and administrative centre in the Madrid region, which made it an established location for large institutional and telecommunications infrastructure well before this campus was built.
profile.research_note: Power figure corrected 2026-09-05. The prior page presented 100 MW as the site capacity, conflating a substation rating with IT load. Nabiax own current page for Alcala Data Center, fetched fresh this session, states 22.3 MW of IT power across the two completed phases with 100 MW as medium-term expansion potential. The page now separates the two explicitly. New per-building detail from the same source, ADC 1 opened 2013 with 7 IT rooms, 4,800 sqm, generators 2N, chiller 2N and AHU N+2, 3 fibre entries, Tier IV certified, and ADC 2 opened 2021 with 6 IT rooms, 6,000 sqm, generators N+1, chiller and AHU N+1, 3 fibre entries, built to Tier III, more than 10,000 sqm IT space in total, fully carrier neutral, 100 percent renewable. Wikipedia removed from sources per registry policy and the Telefonica corporate-history paragraph it supported was dropped rather than re-asserted unsourced. Telefonica fact sheet figures retained. Operator note added, since OSM still tags Telefonica while the campus is operated by Nabiax, and the operator column was not modified. The profile key it_capacity_mw still reads 100 and should be reset to 22.3 by a later pass authorised to change it.
